args: 2_heartfelt and heartwarming, deli man is documentary filmmaking at its tastiest.

3_gruber's sense of a calling to tradition is a common denominator among the many deli owners we meet in this fun and interesting film, mostly stressed-out men who somehow find deep satisfaction in being part of a long history.
4_like a fat slab of pastrami, "deli man" is the cinematic equivalent of comfort food: warm, generous and made with love.
6_"deli man" is a delicious little concoction, a consideration of the history of the jewish delicatessen and how it reflects jewish culture in america.
11_a fairly thin subject for a feature film,
14_the film is content to portray classic "appetizing" as the work of defiant outliers-not exactly untrue,
15_deli man, your legend will survive anything, even houston.
17_in the food-film canon, it aims to the be "jiro dreams of sushi" of jewish cuisine, and if it doesn't quite reach those poetic heights, it's still an affably informative documentary.
8_in balancing the more objective cultural history of delis with a personal profile, anjou serves neither well.
12_an unexpectedly charming documentary directed by erik greenberg anjou that is warm and piquant as well as informative ...
